thread.document:
For Special participation A, I used Kimi on the writing part of HW0. Overall, it was useful, but it also revealed several limitations. Kimi is generally good at recognizing high-level patterns and giving correct final expressions, but it often skips steps, relies too much on memorized formulas, and needs very explicit instructions to produce proper derivations. It also struggles with qualitative reasoning at times.

Despite these issues, Kimi’s conceptual explanations were clear, and with careful prompting and oversight, it was able to provide correct results. In short, Kimi is helpful as long as you guide it closely and verify its reasoning, but it is not reliable for detailed, step-by-step mathematical work without supervision.
